title: New Year's Eve in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has no single citywide fireworks show.** Private fireworks are legal from 18:00 on 31 December to 07:00 on 1 January, and at midnight the whole city fires at once. Where you stand at 23:00 decides your night.

**The one organized party is at the Brandenburg Gate.** In recent winters it was free but ticketed for about 20,000 people, doors from 21:30, a short midnight show over the Gate. Tickets appear in early December on kulturprojekte.berlin and go fast.

**The classic free views are a bridge or a hill.** Be on Modersohnbrücke or Oberbaumbrücke by 23:00, or take the S-Bahn toward Heerstraße by 22:30 and climb Drachenberg with a phone light for the whole-city panorama.

**Firework ban zones exist and move each winter.** Recent zones: around Alexanderplatz, the Steinmetzkiez, parts of Sonnenallee and the Admiralbrücke, active 31 December evening to 1 January morning. The new list is announced in December.

**Trains run all night.** U-Bahn about every 10 minutes, the S-Bahn ring every 10 and the main lines every 20. Count the Brandenburger Tor station as closed from the afternoon and walk from Friedrichstraße or Potsdamer Platz.

**Book the sit-down parts in early December.** New Year dinner menus and the big club tickets sell out weeks ahead, and 1 January is a public holiday with shops shut and the quietest walking morning of the year.
